questions.q: Which standard defines a project as "a temporary endeavour undertaken to create a unique product, service or result"?
questions.explain: That is the PMI (ANSI) definition. ISO 10006 defines it as a unique process of coordinated and controlled activities with start and finish dates.

questions.q: The three project performance dimensions in the quality triangle are:
questions.explain: Performance = f(scope, cost, time). Changing one changes the others.

questions.q: A project whose progress is slow at the start and end but fast in the middle follows which life-cycle path?
questions.explain: The S path: slow start, quick momentum, slow finish (e.g. a watershed project).

questions.q: In which phase is the Detailed Project Report (DPR) finalised?
questions.explain: The DPR is finalised in the planning phase to guide execution.

questions.q: Development projects are usually judged by:
questions.explain: Industrial projects use IRR; development projects use ERR.

questions.q: Which study sits between the opportunity study and the full feasibility study?
questions.explain: The pre-feasibility study differs from the feasibility study mainly in the level of detail.

questions.q: In feasibility, the STEEP factors are Social, Technological, Ecological, Economic and:
questions.explain: STEEP = Social, Technological, Ecological, Economic, Political.

questions.q: Social cost–benefit analysis using shadow (efficiency) prices is the:
questions.explain: UNIDO values benefits at economic (shadow) prices; L–M classes items as traded, non-traded and labour.

questions.q: A fish pond costs Rs 20 000 and returns Rs 5 000 a year. What is the ROI in percent?
questions.explain: $ROI = 5000/20\,000 \times 100 = 25\%$. (The notes' 50% divides by 10 000 by mistake.)

questions.q: An orchard costs 100 000 and returns 30 000, 40 000 and 60 000 in years 1 to 3. What is the pay-back period in years?
questions.explain: After 2 years 70 000 is recovered; the remaining 30 000 is half of year 3's 60 000, so 2.5 years.

questions.q: What is the present value of Rs 121 received in 2 years at a 10% discount rate?
The IRR of a project is the discount rate at which:
questions.explain: IRR is the rate at which the present value of benefits equals that of costs.

questions.q: Risk, unlike uncertainty, is:
options: Unpredictable and assessed by sensitivity analysis
questions.explain: Risk is quantifiable (probability); uncertainty is analysed by sensitivity analysis.

questions.q: The main weakness of a Gantt bar chart is that it:
options: Does not show interrelationships between tasks
questions.explain: A bar chart cannot show how an overrun in one task affects others or the end date.

questions.q: PERT was developed for:
options: The US Navy Polaris missile programme
questions.explain: PERT: US Navy, Polaris (1956–58). CPM: E. I. du Pont.

questions.q: The key difference between PERT and CPM is that PERT:
questions.explain: PERT is probabilistic; CPM uses one deterministic estimate.

questions.q: PERT estimates for site selection are $T_O = 4$, $T_M = 6$, $T_P = 14$ days. What is $T_E$?
Pump installation has $T_O = 3$, $T_M = 4$, $T_P = 11$ days. What is $T_E$?
questions.explain: $T_E = (3 + 16 + 11)/6 = 5$ days. The notes' table shows 3 by mistake.

questions.q: A dummy activity:
options: Shows logic only and uses no time or resources
Is drawn with a double line
questions.explain: A dummy (dashed arrow) carries a precedence relationship only.

questions.q: An event from which more than one activity starts is a:
questions.explain: Burst = several activities leave; merge = several activities enter.

questions.q: In the forward pass, at a merge event you take the:
questions.explain: EST at a merge event is the maximum of the incoming estimates; in the backward pass, take the minimum at a burst event.

questions.q: In the lift irrigation network, event 4 has EST 14 and LST 22. What is its slack in days?
questions.explain: Slack = LST − EST = 22 − 14 = 8 days, so event 4 is not critical.

questions.q: Activity E (4 → 5) lasts 3 days. $E_4 = 14$, $L_4 = 22$, $E_5 = L_5 = 25$. What is its free float?
questions.explain: $FF = E_j - E_i - t = 25 - 14 - 3 = 8$. Its independent float is $25 - 22 - 3 = 0$.

questions.q: Which relationship between floats always holds?
questions.explain: Total float ≥ free float ≥ independent float.

questions.q: A (3 d) precedes B (4 d) and C (2 d); D (5 d) follows both B and C. What is the project duration in days?
questions.explain: The longest path is A–B–D: $3 + 4 + 5 = 12$ days.

questions.q: Starting every activity at its latest start time is avoided because it:
questions.explain: All float is thrown away, so any delay delays the project.

questions.q: "Work expands to fill the time available for its completion" is:
questions.explain: Parkinson's law: the objection to distributing float to activities.

questions.q: Resource smoothing changes:
options: Activity start times within their float
questions.explain: Smoothing moves non-critical activities within their float to even out demand, without changing the duration.

questions.q: Activity G: normal 18 weeks at Rs 35 000, crash 12 weeks at Rs 36 500. What is its cost slope in Rs per week?
When crashing, you first shorten:
options: The non-critical activity with the most float
The critical activity with the least cost slope
questions.explain: Only critical activities shorten the project; choose the cheapest per unit time.

questions.q: If a critical activity is delayed, a suitable corrective action is to:
options: Move resources from non-critical to critical jobs
Start later activities at their latest start
questions.explain: Add resources to critical work or do series operations in parallel.

questions.q: In MS Project, a task with a duration of 0 days becomes a:
questions.explain: Zero-duration tasks are milestones.

questions.q: Bricks are made in batches and building can start once the first batch is ready. Which link fits?
questions.explain: Start-to-Start, lagged by the time to make the first batch.

questions.q: Which solicitation is the most formal, used for high-value purchases with tenders opened publicly?
questions.explain: ITT is the formal method; RFQ is informal; RFP is negotiated.

questions.q: In a Request for Proposal (RFP):
options: Price is not the primary factor and the bid can be negotiated
questions.explain: An RFP allows many methods, and bids are discussed and negotiated.

questions.q: Which contract type puts the most risk on the contractor?
questions.explain: Under a fixed price the contractor must perform at the agreed price even at a loss.

questions.q: CPIF: target cost 10 000, target fee 750, sharing 85/15, actual cost 9 000. What is the total price?
The point of total assumption is where:
options: The client pays all extra costs
The contractor assumes all liability for additional costs
questions.explain: Above the PTA, every extra cost falls on the contractor.
